children: Global credit ratings agency Moody's downgraded Senegal's rating to "Caa2" from "Caa1" on Friday, citing rising refinancing risks and limited scope for debt reduction.
There was a greater likelihood of a default, driven by prolonged liquidity pressures, or a debt-restructuring involving private-sector creditors, the agency said.

"The prolonged absence of an IMF program has increased reliance on regional-market funding to meet financing needs of about 25% of GDP, raising rollover risk and interest costs and worsening fiscal pressures amid high fuel subsidies," Moody's said in its report.
The agency now expects government debt to stabilize at around 100% of GDP through 2028, even if authorities maintain fiscal-consolidation efforts.
The downgrade follows a similar move by peer S&P, which cited comparable concerns over rising debt and refinancing risks and cut Senegal's rating earlier this year.
